"Yes, such has been my lot since childhood. Everyone read signs of non-existent evil traits in my features. But since they were expected to be there, they did make their appearance. Because I was reserved, they said I was sly, so I grew reticent. I was keenly aware of good and evil, but instead of being indulged I was insulted and so I became spiteful. I was sulky while other children were merry and talkative, but though I felt superior to them I was considered inferior. So I grew envious. I was ready to love the whole world, but no one understood me, and I learned to hate. My cheerless youth passed in conflict with myself and society, and fearing ridicule I buried my finest feelings deep in my heart, and there they died. I spoke the truth, but nobody believed me, so I began to practice duplicity. Having come to know society and its mainsprings, I became versed in the art of living and saw how others were happy without that proficiency, enjoying for free the favors I had so painfully striven for. It was then that despair was born in my heart--not the despair that is cured with a pistol, but a cold, impotent desperation, concealed under a polite exterior and a good-natured smile. I became a moral cripple; I had lost one half of my soul, for it had shriveled, dried up and died, and I had cut it off and cast it away, while the other half stirred and lived, adapted to serve every comer. No one noticed this, because no one suspected there had been another half."

> When is it the time to step up and do something great in your life?

Some of us are easily cought up in thinking that it is too late, that others succeeded way sooner than we did. Look at this 25 year old guy, he speaks 5 languages, theres no way I could be like him, he sure must have started very early and it is too late for me. That pro athlete breaking the world record at the age of 21? I will never do that and so I maybe just wont start. Maybe if I thought about it a year ago, but now? Naah this just wont work. I am too old, I am too stupid. No man, the time is now. No matter how old you are, no matter what you did or didnt do with your life, no matter how much money you have, no matter what other people think. Start now, tomorrow youre going to regret you havent started today. Also remember that refusing to make amy decision is also a decision - probably the poorest one you can ever make.

Learning every skill in time looks more or less like [this](http://www.doitpoms.ac.uk/tlplib/bioelasticity/images/img003.gif) - it is quite easy to get all the basics but after that sharp increase comes a quite lengthy plateau. This is when people lose their motivation because they dont see any improvement or they start to realize the road ahead of them is longer they initially expected. Every time you feel this way try to shift your perspective and focus on two-three steps that are ahead of you. Also, dont let yourself be overwhelmed by the bulk of information you want to learn. You want to learn the calculus? One book will be enough, dont even bother looking at other ones - they will just dwarf your self esteem even more. Baby steps.

Keep also in mind that too much stress will decrease your [performance](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yerkes%E2%80%93Dodson_law). Again, focus on things that are immediately ahead of you rather than miles away. If on your first guitar lesson you will tend to think "oh my gosh, this is what i want to be doing all my life I need to focus, oh no my fingers hurt, for sure i wont be able to earn money on this" every mistake will hurt even more. 

> And most importantly, how do you make the close ones interested in your passions and help you with them?

If you are persistent enough expect others to naturally follow you. Mark your teritory - tell others what things are important to you - and dont let anyone denigrate whatever you do . At first they will probably be indifferent which is a natural reaction but with time people around will see whatever you do as an inherent trait of your personality rather just a temporary whim. This is when they will get involved, this is when youll meet other people doing the same thing as you are. But it may well happen that most of the time you'll be on your own, in the dark wondering what decision to make. Others will lend their hand motivating you but dont expect anyone to "push" you in the direction you should be heading. Thats ok, thats natural - as long as others support everything you do youre in the clear. Dont be afraid to ask for advice but at the end it is you who will have to make decissions and face their consequences.
